copy.title: Warmth can differ from overall Extraversion.
copy.body: Warmth is not low while overall Extraversion is lower. Consider how you express friendliness and closeness, then read the other reported facets, such as Group Participation and Assertiveness, separately. This difference alone does not establish group preferences or social skill.
copy.why_it_matters: Low extraversion does not by itself mean an absence of warmth.

copy.title: Lower overall Extraversion can coexist with a preference for group company.
copy.body: In this result, Group Participation sits higher than overall Extraversion. Consider your wish for group company separately from the other facets actually reported, rather than reading the lower overall position as avoidance of every group setting. This difference alone does not establish social skill, tolerance, or recovery needs.
copy.why_it_matters: Separate group preference from the broad domain, then consider available opportunities, what you want, and how the interaction feels when making plans.

copy.title: Warmth and group interest can coexist with less assertiveness or stimulation seeking.
copy.body: Your answers report warmth and interest in group participation alongside lower assertiveness and stimulation seeking. Check when that pattern fits; it is not a verdict on social skill.
copy.why_it_matters: Separate wanting company, taking the floor, and seeking intensity rather than treating them as one ability.

copy.title: Interest in interaction does not require a preference for intense stimulation.
copy.body: Stimulation seeking is lower than overall extraversion. You may prefer some forms of interaction while avoiding intense or high-risk settings; this does not measure performance in either.
copy.why_it_matters: Distinguish a preferred setting from what you can do in it.
